problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}]x(t)
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above.
Find the unknown function $f(t)$ in the general solution to the system, shown below.

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}f(t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}]
$$

*Hint: The matrix has the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=3\text{i}$ with the corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}].$*
worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and associated eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 \\ -3 & 3\end{aligned}].$ 

We are given the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=3\text{i}$ and the corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Note:** The eigenvector corresponding to the second eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{1}$ is 
${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{1}.$ But we do not require this eigenvector for solving our system.

The solution that we obtain for the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=3\text{i}$ and its associated eigenvector is

$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3\text{i}t}.
$$

We now express this as a real function. Using Euler's formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{3\text{i}t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)-\text{i}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t))+\text{i}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}]+\text{i}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}] \\  & ={\text{w}}_{1}(t)+\text{i}{\text{w}}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${w}_{1}$ and ${w}_{2}$ are linearly independent. Therefore, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & ={c}_{1}{\text{w}}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{\text{w}}_{2}(t) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, $f(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t).$
